title: The Freebase Knowledge Graph: Foundational Paper and Authorship
summary: This community centers on the seminal 2008 paper introducing Freebase, a collaboratively created graph database designed for structuring human knowledge. The cluster identifies the five authors responsible for this work and the specific venue where it was published. It serves as a reference point for the foundational infrastructure used in subsequent knowledge graph and question-answering research.
key_findings: Freebase is defined as a collaboratively created graph database for structuring human knowledge.
The paper describing Freebase was published in the proceedings of the 2008 ACM SIGMOD international conference on Management of data.
The authorship of the Freebase paper is attributed to Kurt Bollacker, Colin Evans, Praveen Paritosh, Tim Sturge, and Jamie Taylor.
The publication took place in Vancouver, BC, Canada, between June 10-12, 2008.
The paper appears on pages 1247–1250 of the conference proceedings.
Freebase is cited in later works, such as 'Semantic Parsing on Freebase from QuestionAnswer Pairs' (EMNLP 2013), indicating its role as a standard dataset for NLP tasks.
